snip.t: | Pleural fluid cytology | Is pleural effusion malignant? | Malignant mesothelial cells → mesothelioma; otherwise benign exudate in asbestosis |

| Lung cancer with obstructive pneumonia | Smoking history, weight loss, persistent localized infiltrate; sputum cytology or biopsy positive | Persistent mass on imaging, lack of systemic infection signs, may have hilar enlargement |

| Malignant pleural effusion | Known cancer or weight loss, unilateral, bloody or serosanguineous fluid, cytology positive, exudate | Positive malignant cells on cytology, often recurrent, may have pleural thickening on CT |
Cytology (malignant cells), culture and Gram stain, AFB and GeneXpert, ADA (adenosine deaminase) high in TB.

| Lung cancer (central) | New‑onset cough, hemoptysis, weight loss, smoking history, hoarseness | Imaging (CT) reveals mass; may cause obstructive pneumonitis but not diffuse rhonchi; sputum cytology may show malignant cells |
Bronchoscopy (central tumours), EBUS (nodes), CT-guided percutaneous biopsy (peripheral), pleural fluid cytology or biopsy, node biopsy.
Pleural fluid (diagnostic tap): appearance, protein, LDH and glucose, pH, cell count and differential, Gram stain, culture, AFB and GeneXpert, ADA, cytology.

qs.q: A 45-year-old woman is found to have high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions on routine screening cytology. Integration of which viral genome into host chromosomes is the primary oncogenic driver in this condition?
qs.e: High-risk human papillomavirus types like 16 integrate into host DNA and produce E6/E7 oncoproteins that inactivate p53 and Rb. Herpes simplex virus causes transient lytic infections rather than cervical carcinogenesis.

qs.q: During the processing of an exfoliative cytology specimen, which immediate step is critical to prevent cellular degradation prior to staining and microscopic examination?
qs.e: Alcohol or methanol fixation is applied immediately after sample collection to prevent degradation before the slide is smeared and stained. Embedding and deparaffinisation are steps used in tissue processing for histology and immunohistochemistry rather than routine cytology smear preparation.
qs.s: Crash course part 3 chemical pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A 45-year-old woman undergoes a routine gynaecological screening programme where cells from her cervical transformation zone are scraped and stained. Which specific staining method is standard for this type of exfoliative cytology?
qs.e: The Papanicolaou (Pap) stain is the multi-chromatic stain used for gynaecological cytology to give excellent nuclear detail and stain cytoplasm in shades of pink, green, or orange. Giemsa stain is typically used for air-dried preparations like haematology and FNA smears.
qs.s: Crash course part 3 chemical pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A pathologist examines a sputum cytology specimen from a patient suspected of having a lung malignancy. Which specific type of lung cancer is most amenable to diagnosis via sputum cytology?
qs.e: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung sheds malignant cells into the airways, making it the lung cancer most amenable to detection via sputum cytology. Adenocarcinoma and other subtypes are often more peripheral and less reliably identified through expectorated sputum.
qs.s: Crash course part 3 chemical pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A laboratory director evaluates liquid-based cytology over conventional smears for cervical cancer screening. Which feature represents a primary technical advantage of the liquid-based collection method?
qs.e: The remaining cell suspension in liquid-based cytology permits reflex molecular testing such as human papillomavirus DNA analysis. It suspends isolated cells and does not retain intact tissue architecture.
qs.s: Crash course part 3 chemical pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A cytopathologist analyses a fluid effusion sample to determine if the abnormal cells are of epithelial or lymphoid origin. When immunocytochemistry is applied to these individual cytology preparations, what is its primary role?
o: Visualising ultrastructural organelles at nanometre resolution
Determining cell lineage by identifying specific antigens
Quantifying nuclear DNA mutations by sequencing
qs.e: Immunocytochemistry applies immunohistochemical principles to cytology preparations to identify specific antigens, which helps determine cell lineage such as differentiating carcinoma from lymphoma. Electron microscopy is instead required for nanometre-scale visualisation of ultrastructural organelles.
qs.s: Crash course part 3 chemical pathology: MCQs

qs.q: A clinician performs a Pap smear to screen a patient for malignancy of the cervix. Which branch of cytology does this minimally invasive procedure, utilizing cells obtained from body surfaces and mucous membranes, fall under?
qs.e: Exfoliative cytology involves studying cells obtained from body surfaces and membranes (such as skin or the cervix via Pap smear, urine, or bronchial washing) without the need to invade body organs. Aspiration cytology, by contrast, invades body organs to collect internal cells.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with haematuria. Biopsy reveals a tumour with deceptively bland cytology but invasive behaviour. Which variant of urothelial carcinoma is this most likely to be?
o: Sarcomatoid carcinoma of the urinary tract
qs.e: The nested variant of urothelial carcinoma is characterized by deceptively bland cytology despite its invasive nature. Sarcomatoid carcinoma is a distinct high-grade variant with spindle cells.
